question: Is pembrolizumab in any Phase 3 lung cancer trials, and what are its common adverse reactions?

route.reason: The question asks whether pembrolizumab appears in Phase 3 lung cancer trials (trial registry information) and also asks for its common adverse reactions (drug label information).

draft.text: Yes. ClinicalTrials.gov lists 144 Phase 3 studies matching pembrolizumab and lung cancer [count:1]. Examples: NCT03302234, Pembrolizumab Given With Ipilimumab or Placebo in Untreated Metastatic NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598), Phase 3, Completed [trial:NCT03302234]; NCT06561386, Nivolumab and Relatlimab Plus Chemotherapy vs Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Stage IV/Recurrent Non-squamous NSCLC, Phase 3, Recruiting [trial:NCT06561386]; NCT01905657, Two Doses of Pembrolizumab vs Docetaxel in Previously Treated NSCLC (KEYNOTE-010), Phase 2/3, Completed [trial:NCT01905657]. Common adverse reactions (reported in ≥20% of patients) with pembrolizumab as a single agent: fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, rash, diarrhea, pyrexia, cough, decreased appetite, pruritus, dyspnea, constipation, pain, abdominal pain, nausea, and hypothyroidism [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0]. In combination with chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, the label lists additional reactions such as alopecia, peripheral neuropathy, mucosal inflammation, stomatitis, vomiting, and headache [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0].
